clues: An ovoid tissue-resident immune cell concentrated near small blood vessels in loose connective tissue.
Its cytoplasm is packed with basophilic granules that exhibit metachromasia when stained with toluidine blue.
Cross-linking of surface IgE triggers it to release histamine and heparin in immediate allergic reactions.
A terminally differentiated ovoid cell derived from antigen-stimulated B lymphocytes.
It exhibits intensely basophilic cytoplasm due to abundant rough ER and a pale paranuclear Golgi halo.
Its eccentrically placed round nucleus displays clumped heterochromatin in a distinctive clock-face pattern.
Delicate, branching extracellular fibrils composed predominantly of type III collagen.
They are argyrophilic, staining black after silver impregnation, and stain positively with PAS.
They form the delicate meshwork stroma of lymph nodes, spleen, liver, and bone marrow.

terms.sub: Connective Tissue Proper and Adipose Tissue
clues: A specialized gelatinous form of embryonic mucoid connective tissue.
It consists of stellate mesenchymal cells suspended in an abundant, hydrated hyaluronic acid matrix.
It surrounds and cushions the blood vessels within the umbilical cord.

terms.sub: Connective Tissue Proper and Adipose Tissue
clues: A specialized thermogenic connective tissue abundant in newborns and hibernating mammals.
Its cells contain multiple small lipid droplets and a centrally located round nucleus.
Its mitochondria express uncoupling protein-1 (thermogenin) to generate heat rather than ATP.
A dense, shock-absorbing skeletal tissue that completely lacks a surrounding perichondrium.
It contains chondrocytes arranged in parallel rows separated by thick bundles of type I collagen.
It forms the intervertebral discs, pubic symphysis, and menisci of the knee.
A large, motile, multinucleated giant cell derived from hematopoietic monocyte-macrophage progenitors.
It forms a ruffled border and sealing zone to acidify and digest mineralized matrix.
It resides within shallow bone resorption pits known as Howship lacunae.
The basic cylindrical structural unit of mature compact bone oriented parallel to the diaphysis.
It consists of 4 to 20 concentric lamellae of mineralized matrix surrounding a central neurovascular canal.
Osteocytes trapped between its lamellae communicate via radial canaliculi.
A circulating granulocyte accounting for 1 to 4 percent of white blood cells.
It possesses a characteristic bilobed nucleus and large refractile red-orange cytoplasmic granules.
Its granules contain major basic protein, which kills helminthic parasites and modulates allergic inflammation.
The largest hematopoietic cell in normal adult bone marrow, measuring 50 to 100 micrometers across.
It undergoes endomitosis to develop a huge, lobulated polyploid nucleus.
It extends cytoplasmic proplatelet processes into marrow sinusoids to release platelets.
